 THREE
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE CHURCH
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: the Lord’s Prayer
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to recite the Lord’s Prayer and apply it in their daily lives.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
Which prayer did Jesus teach his disciples?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Respect Citizenship
 collaboration  Love Patriotism
  Citizenship  Faith Critical thinking
  Learning to learn  Trust
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Charts containing the Lord’s Prayer
Flash cards.
Learner’s Book 3 page 90-92.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Direct learners to the image on page 90 of the learner’s book.
 Step 2: Select some learners and help them to find and read Mathew 6:9-13.
 Step 3: Ask learners to say the first four lines of the Lord’s Prayer that they had learnt in Grade 2.
 Step 4: Using questions take learners through the prayer, helping them understand what it contains.
 Step 5: Ask the learners if they will say the Lord’s Prayer from now on. Ask learners to keep their books and
 distribute papers with sentences of the prayer to each group.
 Step 6: Learners to work as a group to arrange the papers in the correct order.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners to lead others in saying the Lord’s Prayer during assembly and other occasions.
REFLECTION ON THE LESSON/SELF-REMARKS

 THREE
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE CHURCH
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Showing respect to God during Prayer
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to show respect to God during prayer by adopting different postures.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
How do you show respect to God when praying?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Respect Citizenship
 collaboration  Love Patriotism
  Imagination and  Humility Self-esteem
 creativity
  Learning to learn
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Pictures of different postures praying, some are showing respect while other are not.
Learner’s Book 3 page 90-92.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Ask learners to sing the national anthem. Observe their posture.
 Step 2: Using step one, bring the fact that as they showed respect as they say the anthem, they must do so when
 praying.
 Step 3: Direct learners to activity 3 on page 92 of the learner’s book.
 Step 4: Use questions to remind the learners that the Lord’s prayer requires respect us to have humility as we honour
 God and accept that his will be done.
 Step 5: Guide the learners to understand why it is important to show respect to God when praying.
 Step 6: Lead learners to say ways in which they will show respect to God as they pray. Using pictures collected,
 show learners and ask them if the people are showing respect to God or not.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners to lead others in saying the Lord’s Prayer during assembly and other occasions.

 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Respect Citizenship

  Imagination and  Humility Self-esteem

Good news bible
Pictures of different postures praying, some are showing respect while other are not.
Learner’s Book 3 page 90-92
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Ask learners what happens when they ask for something in a rude way and when they ask in a humble and
 respectful way.
 Step 2: Ask learners if they have prayed since the last session.
 Step 3: Using questions remind learners of the need to be humble and respectful during prayer as indicated by the
 first four lines of the Lord’s Prayer.
 Step 4: Lead learners into appreciating that just as they are likely to get their requests from others when they are
 humble and respectful, they should pray to God in a humble and respectful way.
 Step 5: Ask learners how they are going to pray to God going forward.
 Step 6: Direct learners to activity 4. Put the learners in groups and ask the to do- demonstrate how they will show
 respect to God when saying the Lord’s Prayer.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question, direct on take home activity and inform them of the next lesson.

Encourage learners to lead others in saying the Lord’s Prayer during assembly and other occasions.

 THREE
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: THE CHURCH
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: The coming of the Holy Spirit
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to discuss the coming of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost and
relate it to their lives.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
What happened on the day of Pentecost?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Unity Citizenship
 collaboration  Sharing Social cohesion
  Learning to learn  Integrity
  Learning to learn  courage
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Candle.
Matchbox.
Laptop, projector.
Video of the day of Pentecost.
Learner’s Book 3 page 94-95.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: At a safe space on your desk, place the candle and light it. Let the learners say if they have ever seen such a
 flame hovering on someone’s head.
 Step 2: Bring the key inquiry questions to the attention of the learners.
 Step 3: Direct learners to activity 1. Have them look at the image before attempting to answer questions that follow.
 Step 4: Select learners and help them to find and read out loud Acts 2:1-4.
 Step 5: Guide learners to recall that in grade 2 they learnt about the promise Jesus gave to his disciples.
 Step 6: Use questions to get details of what happened on Pentecost. Lead learners to discuss what they think and feel
 about what happened on the day of Pentecost.
 Step 7: Use leading questions to get learners to appreciate the gift of the Holy Spirit and direct learners to activity 2
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question, direct on take home activity and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners and help them make it a habit or even form a club that does work that reflect a particular fruit of the
 Holy Spirit according to their abilities..

SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: The fruit of the Holy Spirit
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to appreciate the fruit of the Holy Spirit by living harmoniously with
others.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
Which are some of the fruit of the Holy Spirit?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Communication and  Love Citizenship
 collaboration  Sharing Social cohesion
  Imagination and  Unity Self-esteem
 creativity  Co-operation Interpersonal relationship
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Flash cards with the fruit of the Holy Spirit and others with vices, crayons.
Old newspapers, Colored and plain papers.
Cellotape, strings.
Learner’s Book 3 page 95-96.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Bring the key inquiry questions to the attention of the learners.
 Step 2: Direct the learners to activity 1. Give them time to conduct the activities 1 and 2.
 Step 3: Select some learners to read Galatians 5:22 out loud as the others listen.
 Step 4: Use questions and leading statements to help the learners understand the concept of the fruit of the Holy
 Spirit. Use the analogy of the importance of normal fruits to our bodies to help with the explanation.
 Step 5: Guide learners to desire to have the fruit of the Holy Spirit because of the good they bring. Direct learners to
 activity 5. Put them in groups to carry out the task.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question, direct on take home activity and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners and help them make it a habit or even form a club that does work that reflect a particular fruit of the
 Holy Spirit according to their abilities..
